slides.text: In 1962, two designers made a ceiling light that never touches the ceiling.
They borrowed the idea from a street lamp, which lights the ground a set distance from where it stands.
A steel arc carries the shade out over the dining table, and the base stays in the corner.
The base is a block of Carrara marble, heavy enough to hold the arc out with no fixture and no holes in the ceiling.
There is a hole through the marble. Slide a broom handle through it and two people can carry the lamp.
